To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) the corporate financial policy affects the value and the default risk of the firm, and that (ii) the value of the financial policy is affected by the value of the corporate assets.

(1) the value of the corporation is a piecewise linear decreasing function of the level of dividends; (2) when the value of assets is high, shareholders have the incentives to pay high dividends; (3) when the value assets is low, there is a conflict of interest between shareholders and debt holders; (4) when the value is low, shareholders will not pay high dividends; and (5) when the value if assets is very low, the firm is in a state of distress

(i) when the corporate financial policy has no default risk, the dividend policy does not affect the value of the company; (ii) when the corporate policy implies some default risk, the optimal dividend policy is decreasing in the value of the asset and (iii) the agency costs of the dividend policy are increasing in the value of assets.

the corporate financial structure is irrelevant when the corporate financial policy does not imply default risk.
the corporate financial policies affect the value of the firms, the dividend policy is the most important financial policy, and the agency costs can be substantial.
the corporate financial policies are not relevant in the absence of default risk, while the corporate financial policies affect the value of the firms in the presence of default risk.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a complete analysis of the corporate financial policy, dividend policy, leverage policy, default risk, and agency costs.
the corporate financial policies affect the value of the firms, and this result holds for any leverage policy.
the corporate financial and dividend policies are relevant and that the agency costs are non-negligible.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the corporate financial and dividend policies are not irrelevant in the sense that the dividend policy affects the firm's default risk.
the corporate financial policies have an impact on the value of the firms, and this impact is not only driven by the default risk.
